observation: Self-shaping exposed two close-out traps. First, reviewing before outcome and checkpoint evidence exist produces expected warnings. Second, the blind-spot CLI may still exit successfully when its machine-readable report status is warn. A run therefore printed PASSED while the final report still contained missing_outcome_closeout. The session checkpoint also has to record the log-outcome action because the reviewer intentionally scans recall/session evidence rather than inferring completion from learning history elsewhere.

evidence.summary: The first lifecycle reported missing outcome and review checkpoint evidence. A later run logged outcome successfully but still produced final status warn with one missing_outcome_closeout finding; the shell runner continued because the review command exit code was 0. This demonstrated that final acceptance must inspect the JSON review status, not only process success.

hypothesis: A self-review performed before its own close-out evidence is recorded is incomplete, and process exit codes alone are insufficient when a command has successful-but-warning semantic states.
validated_conclusion: Use an exploratory blind-spot review while work is open. Then run recall log-outcome, record a session checkpoint that explicitly evidences both log-outcome and review blindspots close-out, and run the final review. The final dogfood gate must parse the machine-readable blindspots report and require status=ok; warn is not a completed self-shape even when the CLI exits 0.
